justification: Adds a replace mode to the one script that writes project_brief_rows, plus the pick file it will load. The change writes nothing by itself: the mode is a dry run unless --apply, --confirm-production-write and --backup-to are all given, and it was only dry-run against the live table. Directionality: a wrong swap would empty or change what a house sees in a council's brief, so the old rows are saved first and the swap is one transaction that rolls back if the counts differ.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A replace file with a gap or repeat in a cell's ranks, a cell both picked and named empty, a bad line, or an apply with no --backup-to is accepted; or the committed picks file stops covering 100 cells (10 councils x 10 topics) with ranks running 1..n. Also fails when a rank or provision id is not a whole number, when an empty-cell line carries pick fields, or when any committed pick is on the served skip list.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The live table's own constraints (read with pg_get_constraintdef): UNIQUE (council, zone_group, dev_type, row_type, rank), CHECK rank 1..5, FK provision_id to regulatory_provisions. A dry run against the live table read 442 existing R2 house rows in the 100 cells and 113 rows to insert, with every pick a current, actionable clause of its own council.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Against the old scripts/load_project_brief.py (git show origin/main), the new tests fail: 15 failed, 7 passed. With the new loader: 22 passed. The skip-list test failed (192218 was on the list) until the list was corrected.

pre_impl.existing_data: project_brief_rows holds 8,976 rows; the replace touches the 442 R2 dwelling_house rows of ten councils (ashfield 45, blacktown 45, georges_river 38, hornsby 47, ku_ring_gai 45, northern_beaches 46, parramatta 50, penrith 42, waverley 43, wollongong 41). The 113 new picks are the clauses two blind Sonnet readers chose as stating a requirement for an ordinary house (28 of 30 cells identical on a second run).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The loader was assumed able to correct a cell. It only adds or overwrites by rank, so a weaker old row at a rank the new set does not use stays, and an empty cell cannot be written. Cross-checked by reading the loader's ON CONFLICT upsert and the unique key.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new script or table: --replace-cells extends scripts/load_project_brief.py, the only writer of project_brief_rows (the loader's own header says so). Deleting rows by hand with SQL was rejected: it has no backup, no count check and no dry run.

functions.name: read_cells
functions.what: Reads a replace file: pick lines, and {"empty": true} lines that name a cell with no pick.
functions.input: path to a JSONL file of picks and empty-cell lines
functions.if_none: a blank line is skipped; a broken or invalid line is listed in the bad line numbers
functions.edge_cases: empty must be the value true; a false flag is read as a pick and fails for want of a rank.
functions.failure_mode: A bad line makes the run stop before anything is written.

functions.name: replace_problems
functions.what: Lists reasons a replace file cannot be applied as written.
functions.input: the pick lines and the empty-cell lines from the file
functions.output: a list of plain-English problems, empty when the file is fine
functions.edge_cases: ranks are judged per cell; a cell both picked and named empty, or named empty twice, is a problem.
functions.failure_mode: None of its own: a missed problem would be caught by the unique key at insert, which rolls the swap back.

functions.name: _replace_cells
functions.what: Saves the old rows of every named cell, deletes them and inserts the new ones in one transaction.
functions.input: an open connection, the arguments, and the writing flag
functions.output: a dry-run report, or a committed swap with its counts
functions.if_none: a file with no picks and no empty cells stops the run
functions.edge_cases: a pick that is missing, not current, or from another council stops the run before any delete; the delete count must equal the backup; the row count after must equal the picks.
functions.failure_mode: Any error rolls the transaction back, leaving the old rows in place; the backup file stays on disk.

break_it.scenario: A pick names a clause that is no longer current or belongs to another council.
break_it.what_happens: The swap would delete a cell's rows and insert nothing for it.
break_it.how: Every pick is checked against regulatory_provisions (current, actionable, same council) before any delete; one failure stops the run.
break_it.repro: load a file naming a made-up provision id with --replace-cells: it exits with 'name a clause that is missing'

break_it.scenario: The backup is short or the delete removes more than was saved.
break_it.what_happens: Rows would be lost with no way back.
break_it.how: The backup is read back and counted before the delete; the delete count must equal it or the transaction rolls back.
break_it.repro: code path in _replace_cells: the backup count check and the cur.rowcount check

break_it.scenario: Apply is run without a backup path.
break_it.what_happens: Rows would be deleted with nothing saved.
break_it.how: --replace-cells --apply exits before connecting unless --backup-to is given.

break_it.scenario: A file with a rank gap or a cell named both picked and empty is applied.
break_it.what_happens: A cell would show ranks 1 and 3 only, or be written and emptied at once.
break_it.how: replace_problems rejects both before the database is opened for writing.

break_it.scenario: A rank of 1.9 or a provision id of 240903.9 is read as 1 and 240903.
break_it.what_happens: The cell would be replaced with a rank or clause different from the one written.
break_it.how: Found by cross-review. Ranks and provision ids must be whole numbers (a boolean is not one); anything else is a bad line and stops the run.

break_it.scenario: A line says empty true and also carries rank, provision_id, verdict or reason.
break_it.what_happens: The pick would be dropped and its cell emptied.
break_it.how: Found by cross-review. An empty-cell line may name the cell and nothing else; one with pick fields is a bad line.

break_it.scenario: A pick is also on the served skip list.
break_it.what_happens: The file says the cell is filled but the page drops the clause and shows not found.
break_it.how: Found by cross-review: Northern Beaches 192218 (the residential parking table with 'Dwelling house and dual occupancy: 2 spaces per dwelling') was skipped because the same table lists a boarding house. It is taken off the list, its scan row is marked read and unflagged, and a test now fails if any pick is on the list.

verified: Old loader: 15 of 22 tests fail. New loader: 22 pass.
Dry run against the live table: 100 cells, 442 existing rows to delete, 113 to insert, nothing written.
The committed picks file reads clean: 113 picks, 24 empty-cell lines, ranks 1..n in every cell, no pick on the served skip list.
After taking 192218 off the skip list: OC-29 HOLDS and OC-30 HOLDS (45/47 = 96%) against the live table.
gaps: The write itself has not been run. The loader's apply path is tested only through its argument checks and the dry run, not against a database that can be rolled back.

The checks OC-29 and OC-30 would not pass on the post-write state as they stand: five invalid answer-sheet cells in the hold-out (the check then has 14 hold-out cells, it needs 15), a per-council 80 percent floor that fails on one to three cells (Ashfield 0 of 1, Waverley 2 of 3), and declared gaps for cells the strict picks leave empty. Those need the owner's decision and are handled outside this change, so main stays green; the draft edits are saved in ~/.claude/plans/ce-session-scripts-2026-11-09/strict-picks-gold-gaps-scan.patch.
A full rebuild of the brief by the builder outside the repo would overwrite the picks; reloading this file restores them.

Cross-review also said the loader should filter on is_active; regulatory_provisions has no such column, and is_current plus v2_is_actionable is the filter the serving route uses, so that finding was judged wrong.

post_merge.db_reset: Nothing is written by this change. If a later apply is made, restore from the --backup-to file by loading it back.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run: python scripts/load_project_brief.py data/plan_brief_picks_2026-11-10.jsonl --replace-cells and confirm it prints 100 cells, 442 to delete, 113 to insert and 'Nothing written'.
